column3: Close to the Hebrew; “when I heal Israel” is rendered “When I would have healed Israel,” and “in the street” “outside.”
Close to the Hebrew; “they do not say to their heart” is rendered “They do not consider in their hearts.”
Close to the Hebrew; NKJV supplies “the fire” after “stirring.”
Close to the Hebrew; “princes became sick [with] the fever of wine” is rendered “Princes have made him sick, inflamed with wine.”
Close to the Hebrew; “they have brought their heart near like the oven” is rendered “They prepare their heart like an oven.”
Close to the Hebrew; “their rulers” is rendered “their judges.”
Close to the Hebrew; “gray hair has crept in on him” is rendered “gray hairs are here and there on him.”
Close to the Hebrew; “there is no heart” is rendered “without sense.”
Close to the Hebrew; “according to a report to their assembly” is rendered “According to what their congregation has heard.”
Close to the Hebrew; “and I would redeem them” is rendered “Though I redeemed them.”
Close to the Hebrew; “they turn aside against me” is rendered “They rebel against Me.”
Close to the Hebrew; “I instructed” is rendered “I disciplined.”
NKJV renders “they turn, [but] not upward” as “They return, but not to the Most High,” “a slack bow” as “a treacherous bow,” and “the indignation of their tongue” as “the cursings of their tongue.”
